newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed lower on Monday after foreign-led profit-taking in some heavyweights as the market's focus remained on some companies in the Lippo Group, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index ended lower by 3.65 points, or 0.53 percent, endig at 687.47 points after touching an intra-day low of 685.52 points. Losers led gainers by 63 to 55, with 62 counters unchanged. Total volume was 174.8 million shares on a turnover of 447.5 billion rupiah.
"It seems foreign investors are targeting blue chips to cash out their recent profits," an analyst with Japanese firm said.
The analyst said she believed the index would continue to correct itself on Tuesday.
She said some investors would continue taking profits ahead of the long-holiday later this week for the Lunar New Year and Eid al-Fitr celebrations.
The market will be closed from February 7 to 11 for Eid al-Fitr celebration. It will reopen on February 12.
Another analyst with local brokerage firm said buying interest in the Lippo Group's units and certain secondliners was likely to remain high on Tuesday.
"Like today, there is market speculation that the price of Multipolar and Lippo Securities will touch 3,000 rupiah each after rumours that both will split their stocks," she added.
Aside from the speculation, she said many investors were actively buying Lippo's counters on their fundamentals.
PT Lippo Securities said on Monday it planned to split the nominal value of its stock price to 500 rupiah from the current 1,000 rupiah per share.
Lippo Securities topped the active list with 13.1 million shares changing hands, rising 250 rupiah to 2,900 rupiah.

The group's retail unit Multipolar was ranked the second most active stock with 12.3 million shares traded, rising 125 rupiah to 2,400 rupiah after it won shareholder approval to go ahead with its plans to buy 50.1 percent controlling stake in department store operator Matahari.
Tin miner Tambang Timah rose 250 rupiah to 5,300 rupiah on a volume of 3.3 million shares after touching an intra-day high of 5,600 rupiah.
Brokers said it was boosted by news that Tambang Timah had a serious interest in taking part in the Busang gold project coupled with report that it will announce its 1996 full year result on Tuesday.
Heavyweights telecommunications firm Telkom, cigarette maker Gudang Garam and Sampoerna were among the target of foreign profit takers, brokers said.
Telkom closed 50 rupiah lower at 4,200 rupiah on 2.7 million shares. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
